[name]
[email] · [phone] · [url]
San Francisco, CA

SUMMARY
Founder and Managing Partner of Meridian Crest Growth Partners, a $2.0B growth equity firm investing in software and healthcare technology. Previously Partner at General Atlantic and Analyst in TMT investment banking at Goldman Sachs. Sixteen years of investing and advisory experience; 14 lead investments, 3 realized exits, 5 current board seats.

EXPERIENCE

Meridian Crest Growth Partners, San Francisco · Founder and Managing Partner · 2022 – Present
• Raised Meridian Crest Growth Fund I, $2.0B of committed capital, in a single close in 2023; anchor commitments from CPP Investments, the Teacher Retirement System of Texas and the Yale Investments Office, with 28 institutional limited partners in total.
• Lead the investment committee and a team of 19 (6 investment partners and principals, 9 associates and analysts, 4 operations and finance).
• Deployed $1.1B across 7 investments to date; portfolio companies have grown revenue at a weighted average of 46% per year since investment.
• Realized exit (2025): sale of a vertical SaaS company for construction payments to a strategic acquirer at $1.4B enterprise value, 3.2x gross multiple on a $140M investment made in 2022.
• Current board seats: a clinical trial software company (lead director), a payroll platform for franchises, a revenue cycle management company, a data infrastructure company and a specialty insurance software company.
• Built the firm's operating platform: hired a CFO, general counsel and head of portfolio operations; ILPA-compliant reporting from the first quarter.
• Set the firm's underwriting standard: every investment memo includes a cohort-level revenue bridge, a downside case holding to a 1.5x floor, and a 100-day value-creation plan agreed with management before signing.
• Portfolio operations: recruited 6 chief executives or chief financial officers into portfolio companies in three years; two companies have doubled annual recurring revenue since the hire.
• Fund I is marked at 1.6x gross and 1.4x net as of June 2026, with a 22% net IRR, on 2.5 years of deployment.
• Began fundraising for Fund II in 2026 with a $2.5B target; first close expected in the first half of 2027 with re-ups from 24 of the 28 Fund I limited partners.

General Atlantic, New York and San Francisco · 2014 – 2022
Partner (2020 – 2022); Managing Director (2018 – 2020); Principal (2016 – 2018); Vice President (2014 – 2016)
• Member of the Technology sector team; led or co-led 9 investments totaling $2.3B of invested capital in enterprise software, fintech and healthcare IT.
• Realized exit (2021): initial public offering and subsequent sell-down of a cybersecurity software company; 4.1x gross multiple on a $210M investment led in 2017; board member through the IPO.
• Realized exit (2020): sale of a healthcare payments company to a public strategic buyer; 2.6x gross multiple on a $160M investment led in 2016.
• Served on 7 portfolio company boards; chaired two audit committees and one compensation committee.
• Co-led the firm's software sector strategy review in 2019 that reallocated $1.5B of fund capital toward vertical software; the resulting cohort returned 2.9x gross through 2022.
• Youngest promotion to Partner in the firm's technology group at that time (age 33).
• Led the technology group's associate recruiting from 2017 to 2020; built the case-study interview that the firm still uses.
• Investments led as deal partner also included a payments infrastructure company (3.8x gross, partially realized), a marketing automation company (2.1x) and a healthcare data company (current).

Goldman Sachs, New York · Analyst, Investment Banking Division, Technology, Media and Telecommunications Group · 2010 – 2012
• Executed 8 announced transactions ($11B aggregate), including a $3.4B software merger and a $1.2B semiconductor acquisition.
• Top-bucket analyst both years; offered the third-year analyst promotion.
• Staffed on the firm's two largest software transactions of 2011; built the operating model for the $3.4B merger and presented the sensitivity analysis to the client's board.

EDUCATION
Harvard Business School · M.B.A., 2014 · Baker Scholar (top 5% of class)
University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School · B.S. Economics, concentrations in Finance and Statistics, 2010 · summa cum laude · Joseph Wharton Scholar · teaching assistant for introductory statistics

BOARD AND ADVISORY ROLES
• Director, five Meridian Crest portfolio companies (listed above)
• Trustee, a San Francisco independent school (finance committee chair)
• Member, Wharton Undergraduate Executive Board
• Advisory council member, a university center for private equity research
• Director, a cybersecurity software company (public), 2018 – 2022, through its IPO
• Member, investment committee of a university endowment ($1.8B), 2024 – Present

SELECTED INVESTMENTS AND OUTCOMES
• Vertical SaaS for construction payments: $140M invested 2022; sold 2025 at $1.4B EV; 3.2x gross
• Cybersecurity software: $210M invested 2017; IPO 2021; 4.1x gross realized
• Healthcare payments: $160M invested 2016; sold 2020; 2.6x gross
• Clinical trial software: $185M invested 2023; current; revenue up 2.4x since investment
• Franchise payroll platform: $120M invested 2024; current
• Payments infrastructure: $175M invested 2018; 3.8x gross, partially realized through a 2023 secondary sale
• Marketing automation: $95M invested 2015; sold 2019; 2.1x gross

OTHER
Series 7, 63 and 79 (inactive) · CFA charterholder (2016) · Speaker at the Milken Institute Global Conference (2024) and the SuperReturn North America conference (2023, 2025) · Co-author of a 2021 chapter on growth equity underwriting in a practitioner handbook · Marathon finisher (Boston 2019, 2023)
